newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, but seen supported.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, but seen supported.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Thursday, with gold and silver closing lower, but platinum group metals edging higher.
"Investors continue to be bargain hunters at prices below $350 an ounce (in gold)," said Ted Kempf, analyst with New York based CPM Group.
"Still this is a highly technical market and the shorts seem intent of forcing prices below $350 target, with $340 as the key technical objective on the downside," he said.
"Any sell off is expected to be brief, considering the level of small bar demand at these levels."
COMEX April gold ended down 70 cents at $352.30 an ounce, after seeing a $351.20-354.40 range. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was a moderate 33,000 lots.
In the bullion market spot gold ended quoted $351.30/80, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $352.00 and the New York close Wednesday around $351.80/20.
Earlier this week gold prices slipped back below $350 an ounce, after recovering to around $365 in the past month from a three year low at $336.
But good underlying physical demand, signs of a topping out in the US dollar, and weakness in US stocks and bonds this week, are all providing some support for precious metals, traders said.
Short term implied gold lease rates fell back below 1.00 percent Thursday, after climbing earlier this week, suggesting there was still little interest in renewed shorting of gold, analysts said.
On the other hand, further gains in gold prices are seen likely capped by producer hedging above $355 and the potential for further European central bank gold sales.
COMEX May silver lost 2.0 cents to close at $5.215 an ounce, after trading a $5.275-5.185 range.

Physical demand for silver still looks good in the Far East, with Dubai re-exports to India rising to 31.33 tonnes in February, from 20.52 tonnes in January, according to the Dubai Customs. Re-exports to Pakistan rose to 5.68 tonnes from 2.81 tonnes in January.
NYMEX April platinum ended down 90 cents at $381.90 an ounce, after further gains were made early to a session high at $386.00.
NYMEX June palladium gained $2.60 an ounce to $152.60, but saw a session high at $155.50 early.

April platinum looks to have found support again around $375 this week, while June palladium looked to have put in a double-bottom chart formation around $145.00 in the past two weeks, after correcting from a contract high at $161.25 in early March.

Workers at Russia's Norilsk metal mine will take part in a national day of protest on March 27, but this would not stop output, union leaders said. Norilsk workers are also planning a stoppage of April 2 over non-payment of wages.
But Russian supplies to Japan are seen resuming in the next few weeks after shipments stopped last December.
